limitations: All runs used headless desktop browsers on macOS arm64, viewport 1280×800. No physical Steam Deck, iPhone, hardware GPU/thermal/memory-pressure, battery, controller, or touch qualification is present.
Host load averages and concurrent validation/soak differed substantially. Runs were not randomized matched isolated trials; no causal speedup or regression percentage is justified.
CPU throttling is an uncalibrated requested desktop stress factor, not a Steam Deck or iPhone equivalent. Browser/process/GPU contention is not modeled by that factor.

A local-only access fixture changed password verifier metadata. Playwright routing disabled HTTP cache; fresh browser profiles do not imply cold OS/filesystem/server caches. Second-navigation or warm-labelled reports do not qualify real HTTP-cache behavior.

Historical source-browser rows only: These URLs are ordinary source servers on ports 8771/8772, not the production-policy preview or generated build. They returned 404 for build-info.json and the remote soundtrack catalogue. Production CSP/worker correctness has separate evidence.

The observer measures first observed running state after the UI launch; baseline and candidate have different readiness semantics. launchToObservedActiveMs includes UI click/automation delay and is not a directly measured input-to-displayed-pixel latency.

External rAF intervals are assigned to the previously observed body state. Application cadence and work use the previous application phase (or hidden suspension); the independent work probe uses the observed current body state. Transition counts can differ. rAF callbacks do not measure physical display scanout, GPU completion, or every browser task.

Histogram percentiles are bucket upper bounds capped by the observed maximum. exactP*Ms fields use nearest-rank quantiles only when the bounded ring retains every sample in that phase; otherwise only bucket bounds are reported. Numbers are rounded to 0.001 ms; raw reports preserve precision. Lifetime counts survive bounded recent/hitch rings; top recent samples are not complete-session worst lists.
External longtask records identify phase when delivered, not exact execution provenance. Unsupported WebKit Long Tasks/LoAF instrumentation must not be interpreted as zero stalls.

Historical source-browser rows: Most runs are stationary on the opening route; the CPU input probe alternates safe border movement. No heavy captures, dense combat, jammer encounters, custom giant boards, or representative content matrix is qualified. Final generated-build runs alternate left/right on the revealed opening border, still excluding heavy captures/combat.

Candidate application exports report master-muted audio despite the observer label default preferences. The missing catalogue and muted output leave real enabled-soundtrack decoding/playback competition unqualified.

Resources are end-of-observation manual snapshots after pause, not peak or growth traces. RGBA8 estimates exclude opaque browser/decoder/compositor/GPU copies and overhead. Shared image categories overlap and must not be added into a cross-pool total.

Historical source-browser rows only: Diagnostic instrumentation was requested in every included run, but the baseline has no application diagnostics export. These reports cannot establish the diagnostic overhead cap without matched diagnostics-on/off observations.

The soak page loaded earlier revision 6f19914ba, reported by the operator; its raw report omits source identity. It must not be presented as a 30-minute soak of frozen 72f498abb. It also does not qualify final fa820.

Completed-observation only means the observer reached its endpoint. Baseline runs can remain running while large stalls prevent logical time progress; failures and the interrupted candidate pass remain included.

Prior fa820 cohort only: Final generated-build rows ran version0.151.1/fa820 on the exact public policy at localhost:8775, after task build/test/profile work ended. Host load remained shared and nonzero; profiles were stored on an HFS disk image backed by SMB. No claim of an isolated or representative device is made.

Final diagnostics-on runs report master-muted audio, and localhost public CSP blocks the remote catalogue. Static-worker correctness is separately verified, but these timing rows do not exercise enabled native audio decode/playback or a reachable public-origin remote catalogue.

Final keyboard quantiles and internal total-work quantiles are lifetime histogram bounds. The independent submission-work ring contains every running-phase sample, allowing exact nearest-rank work quantiles. Most external rAF phase samples do not fit the 1800-sample ring, so their whole-phase quantiles remain bounds.

Prior fa820 cohort only: Final WebKit >=100 ms playing-attributed intervals cross explicit observer Pause. Final CPU4 startup gaps equal 100 ms in two runs; >100 ms counters exclude equality. All such intervals and input maxima are retained, not trimmed as warmup.
Both generated-build cohorts: three ordered pairs each do not establish a causal overhead cap; no physical-device or final-runtime30-minute soak was performed.

Corrected1c505 generated-build observations used the RAM-disk webroot at localhost8776 after task build/test/profile work ended; browser profiles remained on an HFS image backed by SMB. Archive preservation began only after timing. Different storage and shared-host conditions prevent a controlled causal speedup claim versus priorfa820. The observed 4xCPU factor is uncalibrated.

Enabled audio/remote catalogue, representative heavy captures/combat/jammers, real HTTP-cache behavior, final-runtime30-minute sustained/resource-growth evidence and a causally established diagnostics-overhead cap are absent. No universal no-stutter claim is made.
